answer_text: Combining compositional phase-volume predictions with a black-oil description provides a more accurate and physically consistent representation of fluid behavior under varying pressure and temperature conditions. This approach captures the effects of individual hydrocarbon components and their interactions, leading to better predictions of phase behavior, relative permeability, and fluid flow properties. Relying solely on empirical correlations may result in less reliable predictions, especially in complex reservoir conditions or when extrapolating beyond the data range.
